newsitem.title: CHILE: NASA robot to make its debut in Chilean desert.
newsitem.headline: NASA robot to make its debut in Chilean desert.

text.p: A robot that NASA plans to send to the moon and Mars will get its trial run this month on Chile's Atacama desert, Carnegie-Mellon University announced on Monday.

The four-wheeled Nomad robot, developed by scientists at the university in Pittsburgh, will begin a 125-mile (200-km) trek across northern Chile's parched landscape on June 12 and give scientists an idea of how it would perform on other planets or the moon.

"We chose the Atacama because it's very similar to an extraterrestrial terrain, with very little rainfall and no vegetation," said Anne Watzman, spokeswomen for the university's School of Computer Science.
The Atacama, the world's driest desert, has the added advantage of being sparsely populated and in the same time zone as the eastern United States, she told Reuters by telephone from Pittsburgh.

The $1.6 million aluminum vehicle will take about 40 days to make its way across the Atacama, travelling about a yard (metre) a minute while being guided by scientists in Pittsburgh and Mountain View, California, who will send orders to the robot by satellite, she said.
Developed on a NASA grant, Nomad is a prototype of a robot to be used on future missions to the moon and other planets, although with some differences.
Using its 360-degree camera, the robot will also hunt for meteorites and gather geological data that will be sent to Chile's University of Antofagasta, she said.
